errors.text: The hypothesis locates the antiferromagnetic interaction mainly across the fcc/C14 interface, whereas the target mechanism concerns antiparallel coupling of Fe/Co/Ni and Ti sublattices and does not require an interface-induced change in the fcc electronic structure.

It does not assign the 1084 K and 168 K transitions to the fcc phase or the approximately 214 K transition to C14, and its comparative experiment emphasizes 400 K hysteresis rather than measuring temperature-dependent transitions in the specified C14-dominant Fe27Co27Ni17Ti29 alloy.

It claims that the already limited fcc orbital moment is further suppressed by C14 proximity, while the target proposes that the small orbital contribution, together with C14 coexistence and spin-canted/pinning effects, can still support enhanced coercivity.
